bio_en: Tigran Khachikian, known among the Balkan comrades as 'Balkan Arzuman', was appointed the ARF's organiser in the Balkans after the party's 1914 General Congress in Karin (Erzurum). Seeing the Constantinople comrades paralysed by Ittihad intrigues, he helped publish a paper that exposed Ittihad's massacres to the world. In June 1915 he went from Egypt to Sofia, eager even to enter Turkey for personal revenge. Fifteen days later he was arrested by a Bulgarian secret police inspector bribed by the Ittihad, and he died at the age of 32.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Death year not stated in the portion read (probably 1915); obituary in Chakatamart.
